newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wall Street gains give boost to German shares.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street gains give boost to German shares.

text.p: German shares bounded higher in bourse trade on Wednesday in a delayed response to post-bourse gains from Tuesday when benign U.S. data were seen as reducing the imminent need for a U.S. interest rate rise.
German gains nonetheless failed to match the sharp 2.6 percent rise in the Dow Jones as scepticism over U.S. stock gains continued.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares ended the session up 54.88 points, or 1.6 percent, at 3,438.07, some 14 points off its session high of 3,452.61.
Gains were spread across the board with just five blue chip stocks declining, including chemical giant Bayer AG whose first quarter earnings report triggered some sell-offs.
Outperformers included drugs company Schering, which attracted interest after announcing first quarter earnings and plans to buy back its own shares.
Dealers noted that short covering in the market, particularly on Tuesday, indicated investors thought further gains were possible but little fresh money was coming in.
Traders said the next key trading level for the DAX index was 3,475 points. Once that was breached, new inflows of money were expected.

In the short term, volumes were also thin due to Thursday's May Day holiday and ahead of further U.S. data, including the Chicago Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) later today and the non-farm payrolls report due on Friday.
Schering rose five marks, or 3.10 percent to 166 marks after it reported first-quarter group sales up 21 percent and promised plans for share buy-backs.
Analysts said Schering was considered a top candidate for buybacks, which are expected to be legalised in Germany next year, as its cash flow position was good.
The stock was also popular as the group was perceived to be streamlined and specialised.
Meanwhile Bayer, which announced a below-expectations five percent rise in its first quarter profits, ended down eight pfennigs at 68.90 marks.
Among non-blue chips, bourse newcomer BHW Holding outperformed on its third day of trading on the back of what dealers said was strong interest from German institutional investors.
The financial services company hit an intraday high of 29.20 marks before drifting back to close up 2.6 percent at 28.80 marks, 2.80 marks above its issue price of 26 marks.
